details.lane_step_counts_note: half_lane_steps/full_lane_steps are the RAW lateral-offset distribution with no physical guard applied -- they include cornering, so they exceed `events` on any engine that turns through 90 degrees inside one sample. Only `events` is the metric
details.longitudinal_reversal_note: the same discrete lane/edge position remapping seen along the road instead of across it: the next sample lands more than 0.5 m BEHIND this one
details.method: per consecutive-sample step, the displacement component ACROSS the smoothed direction of travel (circular median over +-3 steps). A step counts when it moves >= 1.6 m sideways at more than 2 m/s AND the RAW headings of the steps either side agree within 45 deg -- a lane change does not turn the vehicle, a corner does, so cornering is not counted. A track's first and last step are not scanned (no evidence on one side). Normalised per vehicle-km of path, which is invariant to the CAM trigger rate; the per-1000-step rate is given alongside and is not
details.sub_lane_note: steps with a non-physical lateral speed but under 1.6 m of offset (>= 0.25 m) are NOT counted in the headline rate -- they are partial lane offsets, not lane changes -- but they are screened out of the acceleration series for the same reason
details.vehicle_km_note: longitudinal path length, so a jump's sideways component does not pad the denominator of the rate it is counted against

reference.derivation: Zero is the physical target, not a tolerance: any non-zero rate is a known-open defect. Scored SOFT on purpose -- every current MOSAIC/SUMO run is non-zero by construction and gating CI on it would only wedge the pipeline. Promote to HARD once `--lanechange.duration`/`--lateral-resolution` are set and the measured rate reaches zero.
reference.note: Tracked, not gated. This is the metric that must fall to 0 when continuous lateral motion is enabled.
reference.source: A physically continuous mobility model produces NO single-sample lateral position jumps at all, so the reference is zero. SUMO does not: with the sublane model off, a lane change is a discrete re-assignment of the vehicle from one lane centreline to the next, and the local toolchain confirms the default -- `sumo --help` (SUMO 1.25.0, C:/Users/Administrator/tools/sumo/sumo-1.25.0) reports `--lanechange.duration TIME  Duration of a lane change maneuver (default 0)` and `--lateral-resolution FLOAT ... with -1 all vehicles drive at the center of their lane`. The vehicle therefore appears one whole lane width (~3.2 m) sideways between two consecutive CAM samples, which is precisely the signature a V2X position-plausibility detector keys on -- so this is a dataset-realism defect, not a cosmetic one.

details.method: second difference of the LONGITUDINAL speed (displacement projected on the direction of travel, smoothed over +-3 steps), over the exact midpoint separation (dt_i + dt_i+1)/2
details.sampling_note: each acceleration sample carries equal weight; the by_pair_dt_s breakdown is what makes an interval-dependent artefact visible
details.screened_note: position DISCONTINUITIES are not accelerations: lane-change teleports go to traffic.lateral_discontinuity_events, teleports to traffic.teleport_events, and a track's first/last step is a partial insertion/arrival step, not a second of driving. screened_out.lateral uses the lower 0.25 m sub-lane threshold, so it exceeds the reported event count
details.unscreened_note: the SAME longitudinal estimator with the discontinuity screen switched off (not the pre-fix raw-chord estimator)

details.method: path length / track span per vehicle, so a vehicle queued for part of its trip still counts as moving

reference.cite: project-adopted liveness gate (converse of the ROADMAP 'Sim health' row)
reference.derivation: 0.5 m/s (1.8 km/h) sits below any moving road vehicle and above the position jitter of a stationary one. The 0.5 fraction tolerates a heavily congested or signal-metered network in which half the fleet is queued for the whole of its (short) observation window.
reference.note: Threshold is a project gate, not a published measurement. Applied as a HARD gate.
reference.source: Project-adopted LIVENESS gate, added because every other hard gate in docs/realism/ROADMAP.md section 5 is an IMPOSSIBILITY check: 'teleports=0, overlap events=0, jam removals=0' and 100% of accelerations inside [-8,+4] m/s^2 are all satisfied trivially by a dataset in which no vehicle ever moves (no displacement, hence no teleport, no acceleration and, for a parked fleet, no overlap), while the headway metrics degrade to 'na' because a stationary follower is skipped. At least half the tracked vehicles must therefore average above a walking-pace floor over their own track before the traffic panel means anything.
